summary: The Network Information Center asks participants to make enough copies of any manuals or handbooks they produce so the NIC can distribute them. The NIC planned to send them to Station Agents, to Liaisons, and when useful to outside participants.

plainLanguage.summary: If you write a user guide, please make extra copies. The library will pass them out to everyone who needs one.

subtitle: Request for copies of computer manuals for network-wide distribution.

tldr.problem: The Network Information Center needed documentation about network software and systems to distribute to all ARPANET participants, but sites were not always providing enough copies.
tldr.mechanism: The NIC asked each site that produces manuals or handbooks to provide 100 copies at the time of publication so the NIC can distribute them to all Station Agents, Liaisons, and other participants.
tldr.outcome: This became a standard practice for distributing technical documentation across the ARPANET, with the NIC serving as a clearinghouse.

today: This RFC reflects the early days of the ARPANET when documentation distribution was a significant coordination challenge. The NIC's role as a clearinghouse for information has continued throughout the network's evolution into the modern Internet.

sections.title: The Network Information Center
sections.content:
The Network Information Center (NIC) is the central resource for information about the ARPANET. It maintains documentation, serves as a clearinghouse for network resources, and distributes materials to all network participants.

With the ARPANET growing rapidly and approaching 80 participants, the NIC needed a reliable way to get important technical documents to everyone who needed them. This RFC is a request for cooperation from all ARPANET sites.
sections.plainLanguage: The network library is trying to give everyone copies of important instructions, but it needs help getting enough copies made.

sections.title: The Request
sections.content:
The NIC asks that whenever ARPANET participants produce basic manuals or handbooks, they provide the NIC with 100 copies at the time of issuance. This number accounts for the roughly 80 network participants at that time, plus extra for additions and replacements.

The request covers basic manuals, handbooks, and other substantial working documents that would be useful for others to consult. The NIC does not ask for copies of every internal document, only materials that are intended as reference works.
sections.plainLanguage: When your site writes a guide, print 100 copies and send them to the network library.

sections.title: How Distribution Works
sections.content:
The NIC will distribute the manuals to three groups: Station Agents at each ARPANET site (for operational reference), Liaisons (who coordinate between sites and need reference materials for their work), and outside participants when appropriate (such as researchers or organizations collaborating with the network).

This centralized distribution ensures that important documentation reaches everyone who needs it, without each site having to manage its own document distribution.
sections.plainLanguage: The library sends copies to network managers, coordinators, and other people who need to understand how things work.

references.text: North, J., "NIC Distribution of Manuals and Handbooks", RFC 185, July 1971.
